newsitem.title: USA: US foreign crudes subdued with Brent out of action.
newsitem.headline: US foreign crudes subdued with Brent out of action.

text.p: The foreign crude market in the key U.S. Gulf Coast refining center was subdued on Monday amid a UK bank holiday, traders said.
With benchmark Brent crude out of action, buyers and sellers were reluctant to engage in serious negotiations, traders said.
Delivered Brent on the Gulf Coast was assessed notionally around 70-75 cents under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing.
Among other North Sea grades, a Norwegian Oseberg for mid-May arrival was available around WTI/Cushing minus 75 cents a barrel on a delivered basis.
A cargo each of Heidrun and Troll were also looking for homes at discounts of $1.50-70 and 60 cents, respectively, for June 1-5 delivery.
In Latin America, attention was focused on Colombian state Ecopetrol's awarding of two early June cargoes of Cusiana to two separate U.S. refiners late on Friday, trade sources said.

The refiners paid a discount of between $1.20 and $1.40 a barrel to WTI/Cushing on an fob basis, a price that was higher than market expectations partly as a result of softened Caribbean freight rates.
The cargoes load on June 3-7 and June 5-9.
Traders were closely watching this tender to set the tone for six other Cusiana cargoes loading in June.
An equity producer had the next Cusiana loading June 7-11, traders said.
